svg.title: One scenario run
svg.desc: UML sequence diagram, animated: seeding, the scenario clock, events becoming service calls, the plan call, patrons and the simulated bay, and the collision check.
svg.metadata: ["Seeding: on every 50 ms update, until it succeeds, the Simulator calls add_agv (id only), add_tray and add_payload on the garage tracker for every entry of initial_conditions. The SimAgv nodes already stand at the scenario's poses and report them. Until seeding succeeds the Simulator does nothing else.", "The scenario clock starts when /central/report says Dispatch is STOPPED and consistent. Event times are seconds after that moment, in simulated time.", "Events fall due: ScenarioRunner returns every event with time <= now - start_time_. Each becomes one service call; most are asynchronous, so the Simulator does not see whether the call succeeded.", "Dispatch queues the job, calls the scheduler (this is where the refactored code runs), publishes the request and response on the plan_request / plan_response topics, and sends commands.", "Patrons: a patron_arrival event enters the insert queue. Each update offers the front of the queue to every bay; a BaySim accepts only when its bay is READY_TO_INSERT. It then fakes the vehicle driving on and, with auto_confirm_insert, confirms the insert, which makes Dispatch create an INSERT job.", "Every update: the Simulator rebuilds a 3D box for every AGV, tray, payload, bay overdrive plate, charger and obstruction from the latest snapshot, and tests every pair. A carried tray is exempt.", "A collision ends the run: the Simulator logs FATAL with the pair (for example a3 collided with t17) and calls rclcpp::shutdown(). Otherwise it publishes /sim/report (running, remaining events, insert queue)."]
